name: OpenPort Single-Host Durable HTTP Action Lifecycle Profile v0.5
summary: Executable public reference profile connecting the Fastify action route to durable draft/execution records, durable action obligations, stable receiver identifiers, and crash-reconciliation semantics.
claimBoundary: This is a single-host SQLite/WAL reference profile with a synthetic receiver. Ambiguous-delivery retry is conditional on durable receiver-side deduplication of the stable effect identifier. The profile persists action payloads, does not persist all runtime subsystems, and does not establish cross-store atomicity, general exactly-once execution, arbitrary-handler correctness, multi-host safety, distributed consensus, production readiness, or private Accentrust architecture.

checks.description: One application-scoped idempotency key MUST bind one persisted action fingerprint; equivalent submissions MUST reuse the draft and changed payload reuse MUST fail closed.
Only a successful persisted execution MAY satisfy an idempotency replay; failed attempts MUST remain retryable or reviewable according to the obligation state.
Persisted draft, execution, and obligation state MUST survive reconstruction of their adapters and the public HTTP runtime.
A durable action attempt MUST pass the obligation's stable effect identifier to the domain receiver.
Ambiguous delivery MUST enter manual review by default; automatic retry MAY be enabled only under an explicit stable-identifier receiver contract.
If a successful execution record committed before response loss, retry MUST reconcile that success and complete the obligation without invoking the receiver again.
Concurrent equivalent same-key requests MUST converge to one durable draft, one successful execution, and one stable-identifier receiver effect under the declared receiver contract.
The conformance evidence MUST retain a negative control showing that unsafe retry against a non-idempotent receiver can duplicate effects.
Deployments MUST apply access control, encryption, retention, and deletion controls appropriate to persisted action payloads and policy snapshots.
